children: The central bank conducted sell-buy swaps with lenders over the past two weeks, with maturities of one to six months

The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) has carried out currency swaps worth at least USD 10 billion in recent weeks to reduce surplus liquidity in the financial system, according to a media report citing people familiar with the developments.

The RBI conducted sell-buy dollar-rupee swaps with lenders over the past two weeks, with maturities ranging from one month to around six months, the report said. The sources asked not to be identified as they were discussing private transactions.

Under a sell-buy swap, the RBI sells dollars to banks in exchange for rupees and agrees to reverse the transaction at a later date. The arrangement temporarily removes rupee liquidity from the banking system.

Dollar-rupee contract rates for maturities of three to six months have increased this month, reflecting the central bank’s activity, according to the report. Six-month and one-year rates rose by around 20 basis points on Thursday to their highest levels since May.

The recent swaps are larger than similar measures publicly announced by the RBI in recent years. The central bank typically conducts public swap auctions in tranches of around USD 3 billion to USD 5 billion, the report said.

The banking system has accumulated surplus cash following RBI measures to attract foreign capital, which brought in more than USD 140 billion, according to the report. Surplus banking liquidity reached a record Rs 11 trillion earlier this month, putting downward pressure on borrowing costs amid concerns over inflation risks from elevated oil prices.

Gaura Sen Gupta, Chief Economist at IDFC First Bank, said the RBI had been managing the liquidity build-up through bond sales and sell-buy swaps. She estimated that the central bank may have carried out around USD 10 billion to USD 15 billion of sell-buy swaps maturing within the financial year ending 31 March 2027.

The RBI has also used open market bond sales to absorb surplus liquidity. Reuters reported on 22 September that the central bank had reduced the banking system’s liquidity surplus by 55 per cent from a record Rs 11.16 trillion to Rs 4.92 trillion through bond sales, foreign exchange swaps and other measures.
